questions.learningObjective: Apply integer division to a real-world grouping problem.
questions.question: A server rack has 132 units. If each server takes 5 units, how many complete servers can be installed?
questions.explanation: Divide the total units by the units per server and keep only the whole number: 132 ÷ 5 = 26.40, so only 26 complete servers fit — the leftover units aren't enough for another one.
questions.hint: Divide, then drop anything after the decimal point — partial servers don't count.

questions.learningObjective: Find the least common multiple of two integers.
questions.question: What is the least common multiple (LCM) of 14 and 7?
questions.explanation: The LCM is the smallest number divisible by both 14 and 7. Using LCM(a,b) = (a×b)/GCD(a,b): GCD(14,7) = 7, so LCM = (14×7)/7 = 14.
questions.hint: Find the greatest common divisor first, then use LCM = (a × b) ÷ GCD(a, b).

questions.learningObjective: Convert a nominal interest rate into an effective annual rate under compounding.
questions.question: What is the effective annual rate if the nominal rate is 12% compounded semi-annually? (Round to two decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Effective rate = (1 + nominal/n)^n − 1 = (1 + 12%/2)^2 − 1 ≈ 12.36%. Compounding twice a year makes the effective rate slightly higher than the nominal rate.
questions.hint: Effective rate = (1 + nominal rate ÷ number of periods)^(number of periods) − 1.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the break-even point using fixed costs and contribution margin.
